button.intent: A control that performs an action. Untouched — daisyUI decided what a button is, and the theme decided what colour it is.
button.namespaceNote: daisyUI prefixes its button modifiers, so the namespace is unambiguous. `root` narrows it to elements carrying `.btn`. `join-item` is deliberately OUT: it belongs to the `join` container's anatomy and says nothing about which button this is — claiming it made every button inside a toggle group read as an unknown variant.

primary.intent: The action a screen exists for: create a recipe, apply the filters.

secondary.intent: A supporting action beside a primary one. Outlined, so a pair of buttons has one obvious answer.

icon.intent: An action with no label: the overflow menu, the view toggle, closing a panel.

favourite.intent: The heart on a recipe photograph. Round because it sits over an image and needs to read as a token rather than a control bar.

icon-selected.intent: The chosen option in a group of icon toggles, such as grid versus list.
icon-selected.notes: Added because the verifier refused the markup. The vocabulary had `icon` but no way to say which icon button is active — a gap nobody notices while writing the page and the check finds immediately.

size.intent: Physical size. Orthogonal to emphasis — an icon button can be small without becoming a different pattern.

small.intent: Controls that sit inside another surface: a card photograph, a panel header.

card.intent: A recipe in a list: photograph, title, summary, meta and tags.

recipe.intent: The horizontal recipe row. The only card shape this product has.
recipe.diverges: daisyUI lets a side card's image size itself from its content, which gives a ragged left edge down a list. This product's list is scanned vertically, so the images are pinned to a fixed column and cropped to fill. Geometry only — the card's colour, radius, border and padding all still come from the theme.
recipe.example:
Sopa de Abóbora

Aconchegante e cremosa.

nav.intent: The sidebar menu and the section tabs.

menu.intent: The primary sidebar. How the product moves between sections.
menu.diverges: daisyUI paints the active item with `neutral` — the library treating navigation as chrome. This product's navigation carries its only brand colour, so the active item takes `action` instead. Not a colour correction: the theme was right and the ROLE assignment was the library's, which is a decision only the product can make.

tabs.intent: Switching between views of the same collection without leaving the page.
tabs.diverges: The underline is pulled away from the label so the rule reads as a line under the whole row that the active tab interrupts — a printed index rather than a browser tab.
tabs.example: TodasRecentes

breadcrumb.intent: Where the current screen sits. Used as the library ships it.

chip.intent: A selectable filter token. daisyUI has a button and it has a badge; it has no control that is clickable, carries a selected state and reads as a label.
chip.namespaceNote: Entirely the product's namespace — there is no daisyUI class to govern here, which is what makes this a composition rather than an override.

chip.intent: One filter value. Pressed state carried by `aria-pressed`, so the accessible name and the visual state cannot drift apart.
chip.notes: Built from tokens rather than from `.btn`. Inheriting a button's height and padding is what makes a filter row look like a toolbar, which is the opposite of what a filter row should look like.

range.intent: A slider with its scale written out.

field.intent: A range with min, current and max labelled underneath.

parts.mc-range-field__scale: The three labels: minimum, current range, maximum.

field.example: 0 min0 – 120+ min120+ min
field.notes: Wraps daisyUI's `range` rather than replacing it — the track, the thumb and the browser-specific pseudo-elements stay the library's problem. Every product that ships a range writes these three labels; this one wrote them once.

bare.intent: daisyUI's slider on its own, for places where surrounding text already states the scale.
bare.example: <input type="range" class="range range-primary" min="0" max="100" value="60" aria-label="Exemplo">
bare.notes: `field` wraps this rather than replacing it, so the track and the browser-specific pseudo-elements stay the library's problem.

meta.intent: An icon-and-value strip: preparation time, servings, calories. Generic enough that daisyUI could have it and specific enough that it does not.

default.intent: The facts under a recipe title.
default.example: ⏱ 35 min👥 2 porções📊 520 kcal

flourish.intent: The brand's handwriting: the wordmark, the pen stroke under a section heading, the closing note. Pure identity, with no library equivalent anywhere.

hand.intent: Text set in the product's script face.
hand.example: Comida boa, feita com intenção, nutre corpo e alma.
hand.notes: Reads `--app-font-display`, a layer 3 hook added for this product. Layer 2 models body, heading and mono; a fourth face is a real gap for any brand with a signature typeface, and a hook costs nothing for the products that have none.

rule.intent: The pen stroke under a section heading.
rule.example: <svg class="mc-flourish" viewBox="0 0 90 8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M2 5c14-5 28 4 42 0s26-4 44 1"/></svg>

field.intent: Form controls. Used exactly as daisyUI ships them.

select.intent: A choice from a known list.

badge.intent: A recipe tag. Read-only — the selectable version is `chip`, and keeping them apart is what stops a tag from looking clickable.

tag.intent: A category or dietary tag on a recipe.
